summary: 1. Sep 17 total production beat target for a sixth straight day (+4,003.7 BCM, +19.4%), but ore stayed at zero for a third consecutive day (Sep 15-17, target 1,877.2 BCM each day) — the longest zero-ore run this KB has tracked, extending the miss streak that opened Sep 12 to six straight days of shortfall. 2. No ore has moved since Sep 14. 3. Material split ran 100% Stage 5 for a second straight day. 4. MTD total surplus widened to +6.6%; MTD ore surplus narrowed further to +37.6% as the ore total stays flat against an accruing target — a target-base effect, not recovery. 2. 5. EX-253 stayed down the full 24 hours for a second consecutive day on the same fault chain (Hydraulic Oil Leakage, then Swing Oil Level Low/Swing Problem) that opened the evening of 16-Sep, one day after the unit's 49-day swing-bearing failure cleared. 6. Fleet-wide Overall Daily still improved to 87.67% (from 86.26%) on Dump Truck and Drill Rig strength. 7. DR-341's 1,500-hour service also ran a second full day, now showing a committed three-day close (18-Sep 5:30 AM) if it holds — the longest single drill-rig stop this KB has logged this cycle. 3. 8. Blast #17 fired overnight (finishing ~3:00 AM), ending the no-blast gap that opened Sep 16 — area 870-513 with PS & high spot, 26,093 BCM, 14,874 kg explosive. 9. This is the same blast the 123rd pass's meeting-note compile had flagged without a matching workbook figure ("drilling red day, blast finished ~3am"); this pass supplies the figure. Drilling itself posted its first beat in three days (+1.9%), though entirely pre-split (PS) metreage, not production drilling. Survey reconciliation for the same day came in at -0.39% (trucks 24,645 / survey 24,550) — the tightest gap this KB has tracked, on a single-excavator exception comment, and the fourth consecutive confirmation of the file-N-reports-day-(N-1) publishing lag.
